proposal.name: Check and prove Python in place

issue_plan.name: Check and prove Python in place
issue_plan.summary: These six issues let a developer check an unchanged Python application against a ratified model, test explicit contracts for its dependencies, and then prove selected functions in their original modules. They connect the component evidence and Python dependency images already merged for #244 and #227 to real execution, keeping tested behavior, trusted assumptions, and proved functions distinct. Each stage binds evidence to the actual application, dependencies, and verification inputs while preserving legacy projects. This completes #294; factory drafting and synthesis, Go adoption, caller-contract checking during tests, component dashboard views, and evidence-regression CI remain outside this plan.

issues.title: Resolve and stage existing Python applications in their package context
issues.body:
Build the package foundation for #294's unchanged-Python path. The merged #244 work supplies Python component identities and evidence APIs, and #227 supplies requirements-based application images. Today internal/project/project.go accepts existing code only for TypeScript, internal/verify/existing.go discovers package-lock.json, and Python checks copy only the verification project. Extend validation and package discovery for a verification project alongside an ordinary Python application, identifying the application root and named source without requiring package-lock.json, # +nagini markers, or annotations. Support an application with root requirements.txt and the existing standard-library-only case.

Resolve component selections, tests, drivers, resources, and input snapshots against that application context, including sources outside the verification subdirectory but inside the application. Establish canonical, relocation-stable identities and unambiguous path bases without changing identities or path rules for existing manifests. Reject ambiguous roots, missing selections, escapes and symlinks; do not simply permit arbitrary parent-relative component paths. Preserve the established lexical Python symbol and exact contract-byte rules.

Stage a throwaway application workspace that preserves package layout, sibling imports, configured tests, the verification project, and required resources. Bind hashes to the actual staged source and inputs; changes to a sibling implementation or resource used by a check must affect its provenance. Select the dependency image from the application's requirements and recursive inputs using #227's existing validation, isolation and immutable-image rules. Do not rewrite application bytes or introduce another dependency installer. Provide this foundation for the execution adapter in the next issue; unsupported component execution must still fail rather than acquire evidence from declarations.

Acceptance: use an ordinary nested Python package and a separate verification directory, with a sibling import, a resource, configured tests and root requirements referencing a real third-party wheel. Check staging bytes and identities across relocation, source/resource changes, invalid paths and missing inputs; test dependency-root selection and the no-requirements path. Preserve legacy Python discovery and TypeScript existing-code discovery/staging. Update SPEC.md and README to describe exactly the foundation available in this change, under D-0122. Have the merger record the Python existing-code and application-context identity policy extension through the decision tooling; the factory build must not edit decisions/ or ratified statements and locks.

issues.title: Run unchanged Python applications against their ratified models
issues.body:
Complete #294's initial adoption path using the preceding application-context foundation. Connect the supported Python existing-application configuration through verify.Check, verify.Run, language routing and toolchain preparation; the current blanket ErrComponents rejection must become a capability check that still rejects unsupported configurations. Execute the configured application tests and conformance driver offline in the throwaway workspace, using the application's admitted dependency image. Keep #227's controlled interpreter startup, import precedence, fixed hash seed and isolated environment, and reuse one immutable dependency image for ordinary and applicable larger-bound runs. No # +nagini marker or Nagini annotation is required, and this conformance-only path must never send ordinary modules to Nagini.

The driver must call surrounding application behavior, including its calls into the selected modeled component, and read observations from the real implementation. Establish executed source and symbol provenance: an import, declaration, successful process, or a driver's own substitute state machine cannot establish evidence for selected application code. Bind observed implementation calls and their read-back states to the selected staged source, driver and invocation; reject an unused or substituted target. Hash actual application inputs, resources, dependency evidence, driver, model/includes and ratified bounds. Populate the existing component conformance and runtime APIs from actual results, not intended invocations. Record which configured tests really ran and their outcomes without inferring target coverage from a passing package.

Reuse TLC trace checking and deterministic runs. Apply the existing exhaustive-state, attempted-step and applicable larger-bound checks when claimed, preserving their distinct qualifications. JSON and Markdown receipts and fingerprints must name actual bounds, sampling, tools, inputs, observations and outcomes; this stage grants only tested-against-the-model evidence, leaves uncovered components unchecked, and grants no proof or project-wide every-size claim. Runtime/import errors, missing or malformed execution evidence, failed configured tests and failed conformance must fail the gate.

Acceptance must run real Python and TLC with an unchanged task-lifecycle package containing a sibling import, resource and installed third-party dependency: a valid lifecycle passes; an invalid transition fails; a driver that never calls the selected implementation fails; and a driver importing or touching it but recording a substitute lifecycle cannot earn application conformance. Include import/runtime failures, deterministic repeated runs, sampled versus exhaustive/attempt coverage, changed inputs and byte-for-byte unchanged source. Preserve existing Python, marked-file and TypeScript behavior. Supply real Docker integration coverage, with final-head execution by the merger if unavailable in the factory sandbox. Update SPEC.md and README with a usable manual adoption example and the evidence limits under D-0122; have the merger record the completed existing-code execution policy extension. Factory drafting and synthesis remain deferred.

issues.title: Inventory trusted dependency contracts and their evidence identities
issues.body:
Add the shared trusted-contract inventory needed by #294 before connecting Nagini. Build on the preceding Python application execution path and the existing component/provenance APIs. A trusted contract describes a real operation beyond a proof boundary, such as a standard-library operation, map operation, I/O or third-party call. Bind each declaration to that operation, exact contract content, application source or dependency identity/version, and the selected backing tests. Include the actual pinned runtime or resolved wheel identity where relevant, not merely a package name or mutable image tag. Validate references and duplicate or ambiguous bindings using the application path and identity rules.

Extend evidence structures, JSON/Markdown receipts and deterministic fingerprints to represent contract declarations, their source/dependency and test snapshots, executed backing-test outcomes, and links from relying components when a prover supplies those links. Keep declarations distinct from actual proof assumptions: configuring a contract does not prove a function, show a boundary was called, or establish that tests ran. Existing assumption records must remain assumed and unverified. Define a common adapter result and diagnostic path for missing contracts, stale evidence and unaccounted-for proof assumptions; the later Nagini adapter will supply actual usage from its verification inputs. Keep evidence replacement and validation atomic, revalidating retained associations so stale contract or dependency inputs cannot retain successful evidence.

This issue supplies inventory and attribution/reporting support, not a contract-test executor or fabricated proof results. Acceptance must cover stable identities, changed contract bytes, dependency version/artifact and backing-test inputs affecting fingerprints, rejected mismatched references, deterministic ordering, atomic rejection of stale associations, and a declared but unused contract remaining visibly a declaration. Supplied outcome fixtures may test reporting but must not be described as executed integration evidence. Preserve old manifests, independent component evidence and legacy receipts.

Update SPEC.md and README under D-0122 to explain the inventory and that dependency contracts are assumptions whose tests will provide support, never proofs of the dependency. Have the merger record the shared contract identity and evidence policy through the decision tooling; do not write decisions/ from the factory build.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Execute backing tests for real Python dependency contracts
issues.body:
Complete #294's trusted-dependency test path using the preceding contract inventory and Python application executor. Run each selected backing test offline in the application's dependency environment and collect actual test identities, exercise, assertions and outcomes. A required contract receives tested support only when its required tests actually ran, passed and exercised the bound real implementation. Missing, skipped, empty, failed or interrupted required tests, import/runtime failures, and tests exercising only a stub or substitute must fail required evidence and the gate. A successful test process alone is insufficient.

Tests must check the observable preconditions, results, mutations and error outcomes relevant to the declared contract. Bind the observed boundary implementation and test execution to the inventory's exact contract, source or resolved dependency, test and environment snapshots. Reuse the preceding runtime evidence adapter and #227 image selection instead of adding a separate test environment. Report the outcomes and supporting identities in JSON, Markdown and fingerprints, as trusted and tested boundaries, never proved dependencies. Preserve failed and partial evidence accurately.

Keep tested contract declarations separate from proof use: run explicitly selected required contract tests even before any proof uses the declaration, but do not invent a relying component or certify a checked proof-call boundary. Feed missing or inconsistent support into the common diagnostics from the preceding issue. This work does not add runtime checking of surrounding callers against proved preconditions; that part of #210 remains deferred.

Acceptance must execute tests against a real installed third-party operation and cover passing and failing contracts, relevant input/precondition cases, results, mutations and error outcomes, a missing test, a skipped test, a process that passes without running the selected test, and a stub-only test. Verify changed contract/test bytes and dependency inputs invalidate prior support, and an unused tested declaration remains distinguishable from an assumption used in proof. Include real Docker integration coverage and require final-head merger execution where the factory sandbox cannot run it. Preserve legacy Python tests and component attribution behavior. Update SPEC.md and README with a working contract-and-test example under D-0122, and have the merger record the policy that tests support trusted assumptions without proving them.

issues.title: Construct and verify Nagini inputs for selected application functions
issues.body:
Implement the selected-function Nagini adapter for #294 using the application source identities and tested trusted-contract inventory now available. internal/verify/nagini.go currently chooses whole # +nagini files and copies only the code directory. Add selection through the existing component references so a developer can annotate a critical function in its real module without creating core.py or marking the entire file. Construct verifier inputs that preserve that function's implementation, contracts, types, symbol bindings and relevant package context while excluding unrelated ordinary function bodies, including unsupported neighbors in the same file. Keep original application files untouched and retain an auditable mapping and hashes between original symbols/source and the verifier input; a rewritten or detached implementation must not be attributed as application proof. Unsupported selections or context that cannot be preserved must fail explicitly.

Resolve every call or operation beyond the selected proof boundary through an explicit trusted contract for relevant standard-library, map, I/O and third-party behavior. Only trusted contract abstractions may replace those external implementations; do not silently drop calls, effects, decorators or assumptions that matter to the selected function. Collect the exact symbols verified and every assumed contract actually used from the constructed verification inputs and Nagini invocation, rather than treating every inventory declaration as a used assumption. Account for transitive assumed boundaries and report missing or unaccounted-for assumptions through the shared diagnostics.

Run the actual pinned Nagini verifier in its existing separate linux/amd64 environment, without installing application requirements into it. Retain the verifier recipe, invocation, original and generated input identities, successful and failed results, exact proved symbols and used-contract identities for gate attribution in the next issue. This adapter does not by itself grant public gate success; maintain explicit rejection until complete proof and backing-test qualification is connected. Preserve the supported legacy # +nagini marked-file adapter.

Acceptance must invoke pinned Nagini on a selected function in an ordinary package with an unsupported unselected neighbor in the same module and an explicit real dependency boundary whose backing test passed through the preceding issue. Check successful proof, a function-body contract violation rejected by Nagini, an omitted trusted contract rejected, exact used versus unused contract reporting, and unsupported or semantically changed input construction rejected. Confirm original selected-body/source mapping, retained package bindings and byte-for-byte unchanged application neighbors. Add focused input-construction tests and real verifier integration coverage; the merger must run the real suite on the final head if unavailable in the factory sandbox. Update SPEC.md and README under D-0122 to describe adapter availability and limitations, with the input-preservation and proof-boundary policy recorded by the merger.

issues.title: Connect in-place Python proofs and tested assumptions to the gate
issues.body:
Finish #294 by connecting the preceding selected-function Nagini adapter to verify.Check, verify.Run, component attribution and receipts. A developer selects and annotates a critical function in its actual Python module; the gate proves precisely that implementation, executes required backing tests for every trusted contract actually used, and runs tests and conformance against the real application with its installed dependencies. The pinned Nagini environment remains separate from the application dependency image. Ordinary unselected modules and neighbors keep their natural syntax and gain no proof evidence.

Qualify a selected proof only from successful Nagini execution with exact original-source and verifier-input provenance and complete accounting for its used assumptions. Link each used contract to its actual backing-test outcomes and source/dependency identities. An unresolved dependency boundary, unaccounted-for assumption, selected proof failure, stale/missing evidence or failed required contract test must fail the gate; a failed required contract cannot support an effective proved guarantee. Keep declared-but-unused contracts distinct from used assumptions, even if their independently selected tests passed. Retain accurate proof-attempt diagnostics and independent successful conformance/runtime evidence when another required check fails.

Extend JSON and Markdown receipts and fingerprints with exact proved symbols, actual assumed contracts and their test links, original and constructed proof inputs, tool/recipe identities and application dependency evidence. Show proof conditional on the named trusted contracts, tested surrounding behavior with actual bounds and sampling, and unchecked components separately; do not imply proof of dependencies, unselected neighbors or the whole application. Confirm that the selected source mapped to the proof is also the implementation exercised in the application's conformance environment, rather than a second core or substitute.

Acceptance must run the full gate using real pinned Nagini, TLC and the application image on a task-lifecycle fixture with a selected annotated function, an unsupported ordinary neighbor in the same module, a sibling import and a real installed dependency with tested contract support. The valid case passes; a selected function-body violation, omitted trusted contract and failing backing test each fail independently. Include source/contract/dependency/test changes invalidating stale evidence, an unused declaration, unchanged unrelated application functions, and receipts demonstrating tested versus proved scope. Preserve the conformance-only adoption path, legacy marked-file Python and existing TypeScript projects. Provide final-head real integration results, run by the merger when Docker is unavailable to the factory.

Update SPEC.md and README under D-0122 with a complete manual progression from unchanged conformance to tested contracts to in-place proof, including the trust boundary and supported selection limits. Have the merger record the completed in-place Python proof policy before proceeding. Factory drafting/synthesis, Go support, runtime caller-contract checking, component dashboard views and CI evidence-regression checks remain deferred.
